family_intro_headline: They get talked about as one thing, but a silicone that rinses out in water and one that seals the strand until you clarify are doing different jobs. There are four kinds on labels, and the name on the bottle tells you which one you are holding.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair:
PEG-modified to dissolve in water, giving lightweight wet slip, shine, and humidity control without coating the strand. 
Gives lightweight wet slip, shine, and frizz control without coating the strand.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Safe for all porosities (including low-porosity coils); rinses clean with water and mild sulfate-free shampoos.

family_intro_headline: They get talked about as one thing, but a silicone that rinses out in water and one that seals the strand until you clarify are doing different jobs. There are four kinds on labels, and the name on the bottle tells you which one you are holding.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair:
Lightweight cyclic carrier that helps oils and serums glide effortlessly over coils, then flashes off into the air without leaving heavy residue.
Delivers instant slip while styling or blow-drying, then evaporates cleanly without weighing coils down.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Great for fine or low-porosity hair during blowouts/serums; does not build up on its own (though often paired with heavier silicones in serums).

family_intro_headline: They get talked about as one thing, but a silicone that rinses out in water and one that seals the strand until you clarify are doing different jobs. There are four kinds on labels, and the name on the bottle tells you which one you are holding.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair:
Carry a positive charge that attracts them specifically to damaged, negatively charged spots on the cuticle—and repels excess layers from stacking on top. 
Binds specifically to damaged spots on the hair cuticle and resists stacking infinitely on healthy hair.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Ideal for high-porosity, color-treated, or tangled coils; self-limiting film resists heavy buildup, removable with gentle surfactant cleansers.

family_intro_headline: They get talked about as one thing, but a silicone that rinses out in water and one that seals the strand until you clarify are doing different jobs. There are four kinds on labels, and the name on the bottle tells you which one you are holding.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair:
Forms a smooth, water-repelling barrier that locks out humidity, seals split ends, and shields hair during high-heat styling.
Coats the hair shaft to lock out humidity, smooth split ends, and shield hair from heat.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Best for heat protection (silk presses/blowouts) and high-porosity frizz control; requires periodic clarifying shampoo to prevent buildup.

family_intro_headline: Not all alcohols dry out coily hair: fatty alcohols soften and detangle, aromatic alcohols preserve the bottle, and only short-chain alcohols evaporate moisture.
linked_inci_ids: ING-038 (Cetyl Alcohol), ING-056(Cetearyl Alcohol), ING-085 (Stearyl Alcohol), ING-086 (Behenyl Alcohol)
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Waxy, plant-derived lipids that soften rough cuticles, thicken conditioners, and give creamy detangling slip.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Great for all porosities; completely non-drying and rinses clean without stripping moisture.

family_intro_headline: Not all alcohols dry out coily hair: fatty alcohols soften and detangle, aromatic alcohols preserve the bottle, and only short-chain alcohols evaporate moisture.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Used in tiny amounts (≤1%) to keep water-based products free of bacteria and mold—not to evaporate water from hair.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Safe for all hair types at preservative levels; only flag if you have a known fragrance/preservative allergy.

family_intro_headline: Not all alcohols dry out coily hair: fatty alcohols soften and detangle, aromatic alcohols preserve the bottle, and only short-chain alcohols evaporate moisture.
linked_inci_ids: Alcohol Denat., SD Alcohol 40, Isopropyl Alcohol, Ethanol (not yet in DB)
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Evaporates fast to help sprays, mousses, or edge controls dry quickly, which can pull moisture from the hair shaft if used high up on the label.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Avoid high concentrations on dry, high-porosity, or fragile coils; fine in trace amounts near the bottom of an INCI list.

family_intro_headline: Protein strength comes down to size: amino acids hydrate inside the strand, silk, rice and quinoa add lightweight bounce, and keratin and wheat patch heavy damage.
linked_inci_ids: ING-017 (Creatine), plus Silk Amino Acids, Wheat Amino Acids, Arginine
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Tiny individual protein fragments that slip easily inside the hair fiber to boost elasticity and moisture retention without stiff coating.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Safe for all porosities—even low-porosity or protein-sensitive hair that gets stiff from larger proteins.

family_intro_headline: Protein strength comes down to size: amino acids hydrate inside the strand, silk, rice and quinoa add lightweight bounce, and keratin and wheat patch heavy damage.
linked_inci_ids: ING-053 (Hydrolyzed Silk), ING-054 (Hydrolyzed Rice Protein), ING-075 (Hydrolyzed Quinoa)
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Small-to-medium plant and silk proteins that add shine, body, and light cuticle smoothing without a heavy or rigid cast.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Ideal for fine-to-medium coils and medium porosity; easy for most protein-cautious hair to tolerate.

family_intro_headline: Protein strength comes down to size: amino acids hydrate inside the strand, silk, rice and quinoa add lightweight bounce, and keratin and wheat patch heavy damage.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Larger film-forming proteins that patch gaps along damaged cuticles and temporarily boost strength against snapping.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Best for high-porosity, heat-styled, bleached, or relaxed coils; space out use on low-porosity hair to avoid stiffness.

family_intro_headline: Bond builders work inside the hair strand to support its internal links, without coating the outside the way heavy proteins can.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Works inside the cortex to rebuild internal hydrogen, ionic, and electrostatic links broken by heat, color, or mechanical tension—without coating the outside of the strand like heavy proteins.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Ideal for bleached, heat-styled, or high-porosity coils—and completely safe for low-porosity or protein-sensitive hair wanting strength without stiffness.
quick_label_tip: Internal bond repair strengthens hair without causing protein overload.

family_intro_headline: Healthy edges start at the skin—niacinamide and cica calm the scalp barrier, salicylic acid and piroctone olamine clear flakes, and caffeine, rosemary, and EGCG support follicle vitality.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Calms scalp oxidative stress and shows promising lab activity on hair follicle cells.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Good for all scalp types in leave-in serums; promising early science, though human regrowth isn't clinically proven.
quick_label_tip: Water-soluble and completely weightless—won't make roots greasy.

family_intro_headline: Healthy edges start at the skin—niacinamide and cica calm the scalp barrier, salicylic acid and piroctone olamine clear flakes, and caffeine, rosemary, and EGCG support follicle vitality.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Stimulates local scalp microcirculation and helps counter follicle stress in leave-on scalp formulas.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Works well in daily scalp/edge serums; backed by promising topical studies, though results vary by formula.
quick_label_tip: Works best in leave-on scalp serums where it has time to absorb along the follicle.

family_intro_headline: Healthy edges start at the skin—niacinamide and cica calm the scalp barrier, salicylic acid and piroctone olamine clear flakes, and caffeine, rosemary, and EGCG support follicle vitality.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Strengthens the scalp's moisture barrier, soothes redness, and keeps flaky or dry skin balanced.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Great for dry, irritated, or protective-style scalps; supports healthy scalp skin rather than directly regrowing hair.
quick_label_tip: An established skin-barrier hero—especially helpful under braids, twists, or wigs.

family_intro_headline: Healthy edges start at the skin—niacinamide and cica calm the scalp barrier, salicylic acid and piroctone olamine clear flakes, and caffeine, rosemary, and EGCG support follicle vitality.
sub_classification: Anti-Dandruff & Scalp Exfoliating Actives (BHA, PHA & Antifungals)
linked_inci_ids: ING-087 (Piroctone Olamine), ING-089 (Salicylic Acid), ING-096 (Gluconolactone), ING-097 (Climbazole)
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Salicylic Acid (BHA) and Gluconolactone (PHA) dissolve stubborn flakes, excess sebum, and hard-water buildup, while Piroctone Olamine and Climbazole target dandruff-causing Malassezia yeast without harsh stripping.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Best used in targeted scalp cleansers, pre-wash exfoliators, or flake-control tonics; let anti-dandruff shampoos sit on the scalp 2–3 minutes before rinsing and follow with conditioner on lengths.
quick_label_tip: Piroctone Olamine and Climbazole are noticeably gentler on tight coils than traditional zinc or tar dandruff shampoos.

family_intro_headline: Cleansing is a dial, not an all-or-nothing choice: gentle non-sulfate cleansers protect weekly moisture, while sulfates and chelators reset heavy buildup.
sub_classification: Mild Non-Sulfate Cleansers and Co-Surfactants (Isethionates, Taurates, Glucosides, Betaines)
linked_inci_ids: ING-030 (Sodium Lauroyl Methyl Isethionate), ING-032 (Sodium Methyl Oleoyl Taurate), ING-034 (Coco-Glucoside), ING-031 (Cocamidopropyl Betaine), ING-116 (Cocamidopropyl Hydroxysultaine), ING-035 (PEG-7 Glyceryl Cocoate)
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Mild plant-derived cleansers that lift sweat, dirt, and light buildup while leaving hair soft, detanglable, and hydrated. Betaines, sultaines and PEG-7 Glyceryl Cocoate play a supporting part: they boost foam, thicken the shampoo and soften the feel of the blend.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Ideal for weekly wash days across all porosities, including dry, color-treated, or fragile hair. Co-surfactants help a blend feel gentler, but they do not make a strong cleanser mild on their own, so check which cleanser comes first on the label.
quick_label_tip: Look for names ending in '-isethionate', '-taurate', '-betaine', or '-glucoside' for a soft, non-stripping wash.

family_intro_headline: Cleansing is a dial, not an all-or-nothing choice: gentle non-sulfate cleansers protect weekly moisture, while sulfates and chelators reset heavy buildup.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Not a sulfate, but a high-detergency cleanser that lifts oil, product, and residue fast. "Sulfate-free" does not mean gentle.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Good for occasional clarifying, oily scalps, or heavy styling-product buildup. On dry, tightly coiled, or high-porosity hair, look for a milder cleanser first, and follow with a deep conditioner.

family_intro_headline: Cleansing is a dial, not an all-or-nothing choice: gentle non-sulfate cleansers protect weekly moisture, while sulfates and chelators reset heavy buildup.
linked_inci_ids: ING-083 (Sodium Lauryl Sulfate) and ING-084 (Sodium Laureth Sulfate).
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Strong negatively charged cleansers that strip heavy oils, silicones, waxes, and scalp buildup fast.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Best reserved for periodic clarifying or stubborn buildup—too stripping for weekly wash days on dry 3C–4C coils.
quick_label_tip: Don't confuse Sodium Laureth/Lauryl Sulfate with Behentrimonium Methosulfate (which is a gentle detangler, not a sulfate cleanser).

family_intro_headline: Cleansing is a dial, not an all-or-nothing choice: gentle non-sulfate cleansers protect weekly moisture, while sulfates and chelators reset heavy buildup.
linked_inci_ids: ING-113 (Disodium/Tetrasodium EDTA), ING-114 (Sodium Phytate), ING-021 (Citric Acid), ING-020 (Tartaric Acid), ING-096 (Gluconolactone)
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Bind calcium, magnesium, and metal ions from hard water so they rinse away instead of interfering with washing. They are not foaming detergents.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Useful if you have hard water, swim, or find products stop working even after clarifying. Strength differs by ingredient, so a chelator in a formula does not guarantee every mineral deposit is removed.

family_intro_headline: Peptides are precision messengers, not heavy proteins—follicle peptides like Procapil™ and Capixyl™ target root anchoring at the scalp, while Copper Peptides (GHK-Cu) and bond peptides support both scalp comfort and stressed strands.
linked_inci_ids: ING-045 (Biotinoyl Tripeptide-1), ING-046 (Acetyl Tetrapeptide-3), ING-102 (Nicotiana Benthamiana Octapeptide-30 sh-Oligopeptide-2), ING-104 (Nicotiana Benthamiana Hexapeptide-40 sh-Polypeptide-9), ING-105 (Nicotiana Benthamiana Hexapeptide-40 sh-Polypeptide-86)
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Targeted three- and four-amino-acid signal messengers formulated in scalp and edge serums to support follicle microcirculation, extracellular matrix anchoring, and fuller-looking density.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Water-soluble and completely weightless on all hair types; apply consistently to clean scalp skin. Emerging, formula-specific science that will not cause hair-shaft protein stiffness.
quick_label_tip: Used at tiny percentages in leave-on scalp serums—never coats or stiffens your curls.

family_intro_headline: Peptides are precision messengers, not heavy proteins—follicle peptides like Procapil™ and Capixyl™ target root anchoring at the scalp, while Copper Peptides (GHK-Cu) and bond peptides support both scalp comfort and stressed strands.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: A bioactive tripeptide bound to a copper ion—used in scalp serums to calm follicle micro-inflammation and support a healthy scalp environment, and in select bond-repair leave-ins to support stressed hair fibers.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Safe across all porosities and protein-sensitive routines; avoid layering directly with strong direct acids or pure ascorbic acid (vitamin C) in the same step.
quick_label_tip: Look for 'Copper Tripeptide-1' in both edge serums and protein-free bond leave-ins.

family_intro_headline: Peptides are precision messengers, not heavy proteins—follicle peptides like Procapil™ and Capixyl™ target root anchoring at the scalp, while Copper Peptides (GHK-Cu) and bond peptides support both scalp comfort and stressed strands.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Bio-engineered peptide sequences designed to travel inside the hair cortex and reconnect broken polypeptide chains after bleach, color, or high-heat damage—without leaving a surface protein cast.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Ideal for chemically treated, bleached, or heat-stressed coils; works inside the strand rather than coating the cuticle, making it safe even for protein-sensitive hair.
quick_label_tip: Look for 'sh-Oligopeptide-' on bond-repair masks when you want deep cortex repair without protein overload.

family_intro_headline: Ceramides are lipids that sit between the cuticle scales: named ceramides do the work, building blocks like phytosphingosine support them, and pseudo-ceramides are look-alikes.
linked_inci_ids: ING-022 (Ceramide NP), ING-024 (Ceramide AP), ING-023 (Ceramide EOP)
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Lipids that fill the gaps between raised cuticle scales, so hair holds on to moisture and feels smoother. The letters tell you which one is in the bottle, which is more useful than a front-of-pack "ceramide complex."
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Look for the specific names on the label. A good fit for porous, color-treated, or heat-styled hair that loses moisture fast. Use alongside your regular conditioner, not instead of it.

family_intro_headline: Ceramides are lipids that sit between the cuticle scales: named ceramides do the work, building blocks like phytosphingosine support them, and pseudo-ceramides are look-alikes.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: A lipid that helps ceramides sit in place. You will often see it listed right next to named ceramides in fuller, more complete formulas.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Light and gentle. Look for it in the same products as the named ceramides.

family_intro_headline: Ceramides are lipids that sit between the cuticle scales: named ceramides do the work, building blocks like phytosphingosine support them, and pseudo-ceramides are look-alikes.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Made-in-the-lab ingredients shaped like ceramides. They give a similar smoothing, conditioned feel, but they are not true ceramides.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Light enough for most hair. If a label shows only pseudo-ceramides, it is not the same as a formula with named ceramides.

family_intro_headline: Lipids are the fats in and on hair: ceramides are one kind, cholesterol and phospholipids are others, and none of them is just another name for a plant oil.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Lipids used in conditioning and repair formulas to put back some of the fats that washing, color, and bleach strip away. They often appear alongside ceramides.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Good for dull, rough, or frizzy hair after harsh washing or bleach. They work best as part of a conditioner or mask.

family_intro_headline: Lipids are the fats in and on hair: ceramides are one kind, cholesterol and phospholipids are others, and none of them is just another name for a plant oil.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Close relatives of ceramides that you may see in more elaborate, ceramide-focused formulas.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: See the Ceramides page for how these fit with named ceramides.

family_intro_headline: Lipids are the fats in and on hair: ceramides are one kind, cholesterol and phospholipids are others, and none of them is just another name for a plant oil.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Fats the hair and scalp already make, plus lightweight lipids that soften strands and reduce moisture loss.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Lightweight. Squalane is the steady one on labels; squalene is the same lipid before it is stabilized.

family_intro_headline: Humectants pull water toward your hair: light sugars hydrate without stickiness, classics like glycerin do the heavy lifting, and plant gels add slip and hold.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Small, water-loving molecules that hydrate without feeling sticky.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Good for low-porosity hair and for weather swings. Light enough that they do not build up.

family_intro_headline: Humectants pull water toward your hair: light sugars hydrate without stickiness, classics like glycerin do the heavy lifting, and plant gels add slip and hold.
sub_classification: Classic Humectants (Glycerin, Panthenol, Hyaluronic Acid, Aloe)
linked_inci_ids: ING-008 (Vegetable Glycerin), ING-036 (Pro-Vitamin B5), ING-044 (Hyaluronic Acid), ING-009 (Aloe Vera Extract / Juice)
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: The familiar ones. They pull water toward the hair and hold it there.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Best when there is some moisture in the air. In very humid weather they can add frizz, and in very dry air glycerin can pull moisture out of hair, so seal with a leave-in or oil.

family_intro_headline: Humectants pull water toward your hair: light sugars hydrate without stickiness, classics like glycerin do the heavy lifting, and plant gels add slip and hold.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Lightweight helpers that carry water and other ingredients into a formula and make it spread evenly.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Silky, not sticky. A very common base ingredient in leave-ins and gels.

family_intro_headline: Humectants pull water toward your hair: light sugars hydrate without stickiness, classics like glycerin do the heavy lifting, and plant gels add slip and hold.
linked_inci_ids: ING-010 (Sea Moss Extract), ING-016 (Chia Seed Extract), ING-040 (Organic Slippery Elm Bark Extract), ING-041 (Organic Marshmallow Root Extract), ING-047 (Fruit Pectin), ING-048 (Xanthan Gum)
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Plant gels that hold water and give slip, curl clumping, and a soft, flexible hold.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Great for definition and detangling. Rinse well and clarify now and then if hair starts to feel coated.

family_intro_headline: Humectants pull water toward your hair: light sugars hydrate without stickiness, classics like glycerin do the heavy lifting, and plant gels add slip and hold.
linked_inci_ids: ING-039 (Organic Mango Fruit Extract), ING-106 (Cabbage Rose / Provence Rose Extract), ING-109 (Bamboo Extract)
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Water-based plant extracts that add light moisture and softness.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Very light. Found in mists, leave-ins, and curl creams.

family_intro_headline: Slip comes from conditioning agents: cationic agents like BTMS smooth and detangle, fatty alcohols make the cream, and polyquats add a light conditioning film.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Positively charged ingredients that cling to damaged, negatively charged spots on hair, smoothing the cuticle and giving wet detangling slip.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: The slip you feel in a rinse-out conditioner. Behentrimonium Methosulfate is a conditioner, not a sulfate cleanser, despite the name.

family_intro_headline: Slip comes from conditioning agents: cationic agents like BTMS smooth and detangle, fatty alcohols make the cream, and polyquats add a light conditioning film.
linked_inci_ids: ING-038 (Cetyl Alcohol), ING-056 (Cetearyl Alcohol), ING-085 (Stearyl Alcohol), ING-086 (Behenyl Alcohol)
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Waxy, softening ingredients that thicken a conditioner and add creamy slip. They are not drying alcohols.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: See the Alcohols page for the full story on fatty, aromatic, and drying alcohols.

family_intro_headline: Slip comes from conditioning agents: cationic agents like BTMS smooth and detangle, fatty alcohols make the cream, and polyquats add a light conditioning film.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Conditioning polymers that add wet slip, frizz control, and curl definition.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: They can build up over time, so clarify now and then. See Film Formers for their styling side.

family_intro_headline: Oils and butters seal moisture in: light oils soften without weight, richer oils cushion dry strands, and butters and occlusives lock it in until you wash.
linked_inci_ids: ING-011 (Grapeseed Oil), ING-003 (Sweet Almond Oil), ING-012 (Fractionated Coconut Oil Ester), ING-037 (Jojoba Oil), ING-123 (Jojoba esters), ING-042 (Squalane)
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Fast-absorbing, lightweight oils that soften, add shine, and reduce friction without feeling greasy.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Good for fine, low-porosity, or buildup-prone hair, and for light sealing over a leave-in.

family_intro_headline: Oils and butters seal moisture in: light oils soften without weight, richer oils cushion dry strands, and butters and occlusives lock it in until you wash.
linked_inci_ids: ING-068 (Olive Oil), ING-015 (Pumpkin Seed Oil / Extract)
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Heavier plant oils that cushion dry strands and add deep shine.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Great for masks, pre-poos, and dry or high-porosity hair. Use a light hand on fine or low-porosity hair.

family_intro_headline: Oils and butters seal moisture in: light oils soften without weight, richer oils cushion dry strands, and butters and occlusives lock it in until you wash.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: The heaviest sealers. They coat the strand to slow moisture loss and soften coarse coils.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Best for thick, dry, or high-porosity hair. Apply thinly and clarify now and then, because they need a good shampoo to remove.

family_intro_headline: Film formers wrap hair in a thin, flexible layer: conditioning polyquats add slip and frizz control, hold polymers set the curl, and gel thickeners give a gel its body.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Positively charged polymers that wrap hair in a flexible film for slip, frizz control, and curl definition.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Helpful for medium-to-high porosity coils. Clarify periodically so the film does not stack up.

family_intro_headline: Film formers wrap hair in a thin, flexible layer: conditioning polyquats add slip and frizz control, hold polymers set the curl, and gel thickeners give a gel its body.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Styling polymers that set a firm, clear hold to lock in curl shape and resist humidity.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Can feel crunchy until scrunched out. PVP rinses out with water and shampoo; Polyquaternium-69 can build up with heavy oils.

family_intro_headline: Film formers wrap hair in a thin, flexible layer: conditioning polyquats add slip and frizz control, hold polymers set the curl, and gel thickeners give a gel its body.
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Gives gels their clear, smooth body and holds other ingredients evenly in place.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Water-soluble. If it flakes, the cause is often layering over a leave-in that does not mix with it.
